groups.transcript: Converts e-books and documents into a local HTML book you can read and translate in the browser.

Add this app to Windows? You can get a "Convert to HTML" entry in the right-click menu of supported files and a place under "Open with", or also make it the default app for them. Nothing changes unless you pick it here or later under "Windows".
Add it and make this app the default
Drag a document here, or click to choose one

Supported: EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, FB2, PDF, TXT, Markdown, HTML, RTF, comics (CBZ/CBR/CB7/CBT), and images (PNG/JPG/WebP/..). MOBI/AZW3 need Calibre; CBR/CB7 need 7-Zip; image and comic text overlay needs Tesseract. FileDO secret files (.fd-sec) need FileDO.
How many files convert at the same time. One at a time keeps OCR and translation helpers from competing.
Leave empty - lands next to the input

The folder that receives the results; each document gets its own subfolder named after it. Empty = next to the document itself (a dropped file is copied into the app's own folder first, so its result lands there).
Chrome (free): convert only, then translate in the browser - no API key. Google/Ollama translate during conversion.

Source - the language the document is written in; target - the language Google or Ollama translate into. "Chrome (free)" and "Don't translate" use only the source: it picks the OCR language while that is "Automatic".
No key saved yet. Paste it and click Save (kept at C:\Users\demo\AppData\Local\doc-html- translate\google_api.key.dpapi) - it never leaves this machine.
One long page with a linked table of contents at the top, instead of a page per chapter.
Convert without opening the result; find it afterwards through the output path shown under the picker.
Rebuild even when a finished result for this file already exists; otherwise the existing result is reused.
Copy the converter's full log into the log panel; it is what "Send logs to the author" packs.
